'''XLfit''' is a [[Microsoft Excel]] add-in that can perform [[regression analysis]], [[curve fitting]], and [[Statistics|statistical analysis]]. It is approved by the [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|UK National Physical Laboratory]] and the [[US National Institute of Standards and Technology]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=XLfit |url=https://www.idbs.com/xlfit/ |access-date=2023-03-20 |website=IDBS |language=en-US}}</ref> XLfit can generate [[Two-dimensional space|2D]] and [[Three-dimensional space|3D]] graphs and analyze data sets. XLfit can also analyse the statistical data. It includes over seventy linear and non-linear curve fitting models.<ref>{{Cite web |title=XLfit |url=https://www.capterra.ca/software/161676/xlfit |access-date=2023-03-20 |website=Capterra |language=en-CA}}</ref> Predefined categories include: 
* [[Exponential function|Exponential]]/[[Logarithmic scale|Log]], [[Power series|Power Series]], [[Sigmoid function|Sigmoidal]], [[Hyperbolic function|Hyperbolic]], Yield Density, [[Linear]], [[Polynomial]], [[Dose-response relationship|Dose Response]], [[Pharmacology]], Equilibrium and [[Enzyme inhibitor|Inhibition]].
* [[Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm|Levenberg-Marquardt fitting algorithm]].

A range of [[Statistics|statistical]] calculations can also be applied to the data from within the [[spreadsheet]]. Example statistics include:{{Explain|date=September 2022}}
* [[F-test|''F''-test]] and [[t-test|''t''-test]]
* [[Area under the curve]] / [[Receiver operating characteristic|ROC]]
* [[Confidence interval]]s
* Error values relating to parameter values or any point on the curve.

Available statistical models include [[Spearman's rank correlation]]s, [[Student's t-test|Student's ''t''-test]], [[Mann–Whitney U test|Mann–Whitney ''U'' test]], [[least squares]], and [[ANOVA]], among others.{{citation needed|date=September 2022}} A model editor also allows users to add their own models and statistics to the ones provided.

== Usage ==
XLfit was validated by The UK National Physical Laboratory<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.engineeringtalk.com/news/ade/ade261.html|title=Home|access-date=2009-03-12|archive-date=2008-07-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080725171006/http://www.engineeringtalk.com/news/ade/ade261.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 2004; the unit tests for this are provided in the model editor from version 5.4 onwards to allow each version to be easily validated.

XLfit was used by [[NASA]] to analyze the battery life of the [[Curiosity (rover)|Curiosity Mars Lander]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NASA uses XLfit|url=http://www.pcadvisor.co.uk/news/software/nasa-uses-idbs-tool-analyse-battery-life-for-mars-mission-3354337/|website=PC Advisor}}</ref>

== Licenses ==
XLift is a [[proprietary software]]. It offers the following licensing options. 
* XLfit 5 Commercial License 
* XLfit 5 Academic License
* E-learning
